name: AI SEO Masterclass - Module 1 Traditional SEO Foundations
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-08

# Summary
"AI models crawl the same web that Google does." Module 1 covers the fundamentals that both Google and LLMs depend on: technical health, on-page structure, off-page signals, the 80/20 of SEO, what the 2024 to 2026 algorithm updates rewarded, and a pre-flight checklist.

# Key concepts
- **Technical:** Core Web Vitals (LCP under 2.5s, INP/FID, CLS under 0.1), mobile-first design, clean lowercase hyphenated URLs with canonicals, HTTPS, XML sitemap submitted to GSC and Bing, robots.txt that allows CSS/JS and links the sitemap.
- **Schema matters more for AI:** Organization, LocalBusiness, Article/BlogPosting, FAQPage, HowTo, Review. FAQPage and HowTo are called the most skipped and most useful for AI citation.
- **On-page:** keyword near the start of a title under 60 characters, one H1, H2/H3 hierarchy, unique 150 to 160 character metas, descriptive internal anchors, every key page within 3 clicks, optimized images (descriptive names, alt text, WebP).
- **Content depth targets:** informational 1,500+ words, comparisons 2,500+, "Best X" listicles 2,000 to 3,000+.
- **Off-page:** relevant editorial backlinks, unlinked brand mentions (valuable for AI), social signals, consistent NAP citations.

# The 80/20 list
1. Content that answers questions directly.
2. Strong internal linking (3 to 5 related links per new piece; update old posts to link to new ones).
3. Structured data.
4. Consistent NAP (local).
5. Regular content updates.

# 2024 to 2026 updates (per the lesson)
- March, August and November 2024 core updates hit scaled AI content, thin affiliate reviews and generic "SEO content". Site reputation abuse actions hit Forbes Advisor and Outlook India.
- Survived: original data, genuine expertise, updated content, structured listicles, local business content, UGC (Reddit, forums).

# Checklist (condensed)
- Speed under 3s, mobile tested on real devices, schema validated, sitemap in GSC, no GSC indexing errors, CWV passing.
- FAQ section (8 to 12 questions) and table of contents on long pages, author bylines, strong About page (E-E-A-T).
- 7-day audit plan: technical, content, backlinks, competitors, then fixes.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Matches TAG practice: one H1 (see the Alphalete duplicate H1 issue), FAQ schema that matches visible content, internal links in every blog per [SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards).
- Schema and titles on Pipeliners and Alphalete are controlled through OTTO in [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas), so fixes go there, not into WordPress meta.
- Indexing health checks run through [Google Search Console](lib:brain-google-search-console) and the [GSC Indexing Tracker](lib:brain-gsc-indexing-tracker).
